# tinypipe

> Execution graphs from Restricted Python. Compile `def graph(...)` functions into a typed DAG,
> run them through a lightweight VM, version/deploy/rollback them, pause/resume, and audit every step.

Use this file as the primary context for writing tinypipe graphs (DSL) and driving the CLI.
The full README (repo root) has deeper examples; this file is the compressed, LLM-optimized version.

## What tinypipe is

- A **compiler** that turns a restricted subset of Python into an `ExecutionPlan` (DAG of typed nodes:
  `Input`, `Calc`, `Decide`, `Act`, `Parallel`, `Loop`, `Merge`, `Call`, `Return`, ...).
- A **VM** that interprets the compiled plan (FlatBuffers binary) with pause/resume at node granularity.
- **Storage**: SQLite (default `./tinypipe.db`, override `TINYPIPE_DB`). Everything is versioned:
  every `update`/`rollback` creates a new immutable version; `graphs.last_event` records
  `deploy: vN` / `rollback: vN` / `fork: <parent>`.
- **Tools**: built-in callable services (HTTP, JSON, SQLite, env, math, ...).
- **Remote tools (daemon)**: `tinypipe-daemon` (gRPC, default `127.0.0.1:50051`)
  hosts workers from ANY language. Workers connect OUTBOUND via bidi stream and
  register tools (`registered_tools` as first message); the CLI bridges them into
  the registry at execute/resume time (built-in names win). Go SDK + sample:
  `examples/go-worker/` (send_email, text.reverse).
- **Daemon auth (default ON)**: workers must send the daemon's API key in their
  registration message. Set `TINYPIPE_DAEMON_API_KEY` (or `--api-key`) on both
  sides; without one the daemon generates a random key and logs it (WARN).
  Disable with `--no-auth` / `TINYPIPE_DAEMON_NO_AUTH=1` (open network only).
  Go SDK: `Worker.SetAPIKey(...)` / `TINYPIPE_DAEMON_API_KEY` env.
- **HTTP server**: `tinypipe-server` exposes the full CLI surface over REST
  (axum). Graphs publish at the site ROOT via META `http_*` keys; the management
  API lives under `/api`. Static-graph execution is open; mutations require a
  bearer token (`TINYPIPE_SERVER_TOKEN`). Audit is OFF by default
  (`TINYPIPE_SERVER_AUDIT=1` to record executions). Blocking tools run on a
  thread pool; nothing blocks concurrent requests.
- **Subgraphs**: graphs calling other graphs via `call("subgraph:<name>", ...)`.
- **Roles**: 6 profiles (pm, ba, ceo, architect, senior, devops) that drive plan rendering
  (`--view`, `--direction`) and `report` sections.

## CLI (fast reference)

| Command | Notes |
|---|---|
| `tinypipe-cli check "<code>"` | Validate without saving. Code arg uses `\n` escapes for newlines. |
| `tinypipe-cli create <name> "<code>"` | Compile + save (v1). Name must be unique. |
| `tinypipe-cli update <id> "<code>"` | New version (immutable history). |
| `tinypipe-cli deploy <id> [version]` | Set active version. |
| `tinypipe-cli rollback <id> <version>` | Restore old code as a NEW version. |
| `tinypipe-cli versions <id>` | Version history. |
| `tinypipe-cli execute <id> '<json>' [--pause-after N] [--env K=V] [--env-file .env] [--no-env-check]` | Run. `--pause-after N` saves a checkpoint. |
| `tinypipe-cli resume <execution_id> [--max-nodes N]` | Continue a paused execution. |
| `tinypipe-cli scheduler run [--max-nodes N]` | Step ALL paused executions forward. |
| `tinypipe-cli executions list <id>` / `executions show <id>` | Execution records + per-node steps (real durations). |
| `tinypipe-cli plan <id> [version] [--format text\|mermaid\|dot] [--view full\|summary\|layers] [--direction td\|lr] [--profile <name>]` | Render compiled plan. |
| `tinypipe-cli report [--profile <name>] [--env ...]` | Role-based portfolio report (executions, error rates, p95, tools, endpoints, env, churn). Default profile: `senior`. |
| `tinypipe-cli profiles list\|show\|create\|delete` | Built-in: pm, ba, ceo, architect, senior, devops. Built-ins cannot be overwritten/deleted. |
| `tinypipe-cli tools list` | Built-in + daemon tools (if `tinypipe-daemon` is running). |
| `tinypipe-cli tools test <name> '<json args>' [--kwargs '<json>'] [--env K=V]` | Run any registered tool directly (remote ones go through the daemon). |
| `tinypipe-cli daemon status [addr]` | Daemon health + registered worker tools. |
| `tinypipe-cli list` | All graphs. |

Remote tool conventions:

- Daemon addr: `TINYPIPE_DAEMON_ADDR` (default `127.0.0.1:50051`); set
  `TINYPIPE_NO_DAEMON=1` to skip remote registration entirely.
- From the DSL, call remote tools exactly like built-ins: `call("text.reverse", value=s)`
  (the language passes named params as kwargs; positional args arrive via
  `tools test`-style calls, so robust workers accept both).
- Remote calls in graphs work in `execute`/`resume`/`scheduler`; a dead daemon
  produces an actionable error. Worker disconnect → pending tasks fail-fast,
  tools disappear from `tools list`.

`<id>` accepts either the UUID or the graph name.

## HTTP server (fast reference)

```bash
TINYPIPE_SERVER_TOKEN=secret tinypipe-server   # addr: TINYPIPE_SERVER_ADDR (default 127.0.0.1:8080)
```

Publishing = `http_*` keys in `META(...)` (META only accepts string/number/list
literals, so booleans are written as strings: `http_public="true"`). **All or
nothing:** if ANY `http_*` key is present, all five below must be defined — no
defaults, no fallbacks (missing → hard error listing the missing keys):

| META key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `http_route` | root-level path (leading `/` optional); `api`/`healthz`/`assets`/`static` prefixes reserved |
| `http_method` | required, no default: `"GET"`/`"POST"`/`"PUT"`/`"PATCH"`/`"DELETE"`/`"HEAD"`; `"OPTIONS"` rejected (auto-served); invalid → hard error |
| `http_public` | `"true"` → no token required |
| `http_timeout_ms` | VM timeout override (0 = plan default) |
| `http_cache_ttl` | response cache seconds for GET/HEAD/DELETE (0 = off); header `X-Tinypipe-Cache: HIT` |

Inputs per method: GET/HEAD/DELETE → query params; POST/PUT/PATCH → JSON body.
HEAD executes like GET, returns headers only (no body). OPTIONS never executes
the graph — published paths answer CORS preflight automatically (204 + `Allow`).
**Header isolation:** published routes never read request headers — inputs come
only from query/body and env is always empty, so `Authorization`/`Cookie` can
never reach the graph. Wrong method → 405 + `Allow` header. The same (path,
method) pair can never be published twice: create/update → 409, and
deploy/rollback to a conflicting version → 409 *before* the mutation is
written. Different methods can share a path from different graphs. Invalid
`http_*` keys / missing keys / reserved paths → startup fails fast for existing
graphs, or 400/409 on create/update.

Endpoint map (CLI → REST):

| CLI | Endpoint | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| check | `POST /api/check` | token |
| create | `POST /api/graphs` | token |
| update | `PUT /api/graphs/{id}` | token |
| deploy / rollback | `POST /api/graphs/{id}/deploy` · `.../rollback` | token |
| versions / list | `GET /api/graphs/{id}/versions` · `GET /api/graphs` | open |
| execute | `POST /api/graphs/{id}/execute` | open |
| resume / scheduler | `POST /api/executions/{id}/resume` · `POST /api/scheduler/run` | token |
| executions | `GET /api/executions?graph_id=` · `GET /api/executions/{id}` | token |
| plan / report | `GET /api/graphs/{id}/plan?format=&view=&direction=&profile=` · `GET /api/report?profile=&env=K=V` | token |
| profiles | `GET`/`POST`/`DELETE /api/profiles/{name}` | token |
| tools | `GET /api/tools` (open) · `POST /api/tools/test` (token) | mixed |
| daemon | `GET /api/daemon/status?addr=` | open |
| dynamic code | `POST /api/run` `{code, inputs?, env?, pause_after?}` — compiled + LRU-cached (64), no audit | token |
| health | `GET /healthz` | open |

Execution responses: `{status: completed|paused|failed, execution_id,
duration_us, nodes_executed, output?, error?}` (paused → 202, failed → 422,
mutation compile errors → 400, route conflicts → 409). Pause/resume/scheduler
and execution history require `TINYPIPE_SERVER_AUDIT=1`; with audit off no
request writes to the DB (paused responses are returned but cannot be resumed).

## The DSL — restricted Python

One function named `graph`. Everything is a pure dataflow: no control-flow side effects
beyond the DAG. **Allowed:** arithmetic, comparisons, boolean ops, `if/elif/else`,
bounded `for i in range(...)`, `call("tool", ...)`, dict/array literals, subscripting
with any key expression (`d["key"]`, `items[0]`, `items[i]`, `items[a + b]`,
`items[obj.attr]`, nested `d["a"]["b"]`, chains `items[i].name`; negative indices
use Python semantics `len + i`), attribute access on results (`resp.body`, `users.count`),
string concatenation with `+` (NO f-strings — `"..." + x` is the idiom).

**Subscript semantics are STRICT:** missing key / out-of-bounds index / subscripting
`null` → runtime error. For optional lookups use the lenient tools:
`call("array.find", array=items, key="product_id", value=101)` → first match or `null`;
`call("dict.get", obj=d, key="x", default=0)` → value, default, or `null`. Check
`null` with `== null`. Slicing (`items[a:b]`) is forbidden.

**Forbidden (compiler rejects):** `import`, `class`, `lambda`, `while`, `try/except`, `async`,
comprehensions, f-strings, walrus `:=`, `global`, `nonlocal`, `yield`, `del`, decorators,
nested functions, slicing (`items[a:b]`), `**kwargs`.

### Module-level metadata: `META(...)`

Before `def graph`, at module level. Keyword args only; values must be constant literals
(strings, numbers, booleans, or lists of constants). Stored as JSON graph metadata.

```python
META(title="Seed dashboard", sla_ms=5000, tags=["seeds", "demo"])

def graph(user_id: int):
    return user_id
```

### Logical grouping: `with GROUP("Label"):`

Purely structural — wraps statements into named groups shown in plan dumps and
collapsed in `--view summary` renderings. No runtime semantics.

```python
def graph():
    with GROUP("Seeding"):
        users = call("subgraph:seed_users")
    with GROUP("Output"):
        return users
```

### Parallel branches: `with parallel() as p:` / `with PARALLEL() as p:`

Each `p.act("tool", ...)` runs in its own thread. Branches get **isolated scopes**:
`set()` inside a branch stays local; MERGE combines them (default: last writer wins).
If all branches only READ shared state, results are trivially mergeable.

```python
def graph(x: int, y: int):
    with parallel() as p:
        p.act("process", value=x)
        p.act("process", value=y)
    return 0
```

### Loops

Only `for i in range(n)` where `n` is bounded at runtime by a value (literal or `len(x)`).
Loop bodies can end with a bare `call(...)`; constants feeding the body are cached.
No `while`, no `break`/`continue` mutation of arbitrary variables.

### Subgraph calls

```python
def graph(user_id: int):
    users = call("subgraph:seed_users")                    # no args — child needs no input
    posts = call("subgraph:seed_posts", user_id=user_id)   # explicit kwargs → child inputs
    return {"users": users.count, "posts": posts.count}
```

Semantics: explicit kwargs are passed to the child's input context (overriding inherited
vars); the caller's full context is inherited otherwise. The child's `return` becomes the
call value; child internals merge into the caller context. Recursion depth limit: 5.

## Built-in tools (call("name", **kwargs))

| Tool | Signature / behavior |
|---|---|
| `http_request` | `url`, `method` (GET default), `headers` (object), `body` (string), `timeout_secs`. Returns `{status, body, headers}` — use `resp.body` (string), `resp.status` (int). |
| `json.parse` | `json` (string) → parsed JSON value (arrays/objects/numbers/strings/bools). |
| `array.len` | `array` → element count. |
| `array.count_where` | `array`, `key` (string), `value` → count of items where `item[key] == value`. |
| `array.find` | `array`, `key` (string), `value` → first item where `item[key] == value`, or `null` (cross-type numeric equality; lenient — for "may not exist" lookups). |
| `dict.get` | `obj`, `key` (string/int), optional `default` → value, `default`, or `null` (lenient). |
| `list.get` | `array`, `index` → element at index (errors on out of bounds). |
| `string.len` | → string length. |
| `math.add` / `math.mul` | `a`, `b` → arithmetic (use `+`/`*` in expressions instead when possible). |
| `env.get` | `key`, optional `default`. Literal string keys are statically detected; dynamic keys skip the pre-check and fail at runtime if missing. |
| `env.template` | `value` with `${KEY}`, `${KEY:-default}`, `{{KEY}}` placeholders → resolved string. |
| `env.list` | → list of `{key, value}` pairs. |
| `sqlite.query` | `db` (default `:memory:`; a file path shares state across calls), `query`. SELECT → array of row objects; DDL/DML → `{changes, last_insert_rowid}`. |
| `postgres` | Query with params (blocking NoTLS). |
| `echo` | Pass-through/debug. |
| `test.*` | `test.sleep`, `test.error`, `test.large` — testing only. |
| remote via daemon | Any tool registered by a connected worker (e.g. `send_email`, `text.reverse` from the Go example). |

**Env check:** `execute`/`resume`/`scheduler` validate required env vars of the root graph
AND all transitive subgraphs BEFORE running; missing vars abort with a list.
Precedence: `--env K=V` overrides → `--env-file` → OS env. Use `--no-env-check` only for
dynamic-key graphs.

## Canonical example: composed seed pipeline

```python
META(title="Dashboard seeds", sla_ms=10000)

def graph(user_id: int):
    users = call("subgraph:seed_users")
    posts = call("subgraph:seed_posts", user_id=user_id)
    todos = call("subgraph:seed_todos", user_id=user_id)
    total = 0
    for i in range(len(posts.items)):
        p = call("list.get", array=posts.items, index=i)
        c = call("subgraph:seed_comments", post_id=p.id)
        total = total + c.count
    return {"users": users.count, "posts": posts.count, "comments": total}
```

Workflow to materialize it:

```bash
tinypipe-cli create seed_users '<code>'      # leaf graphs first
tinypipe-cli create seed_comments '<code>'
tinypipe-cli create dashboard_seeds '<parent code>'
tinypipe-cli execute dashboard_seeds '{"user_id": 1}' --env-file .env
tinypipe-cli plan dashboard_seeds --profile architect --format mermaid
tinypipe-cli report --profile devops
tinypipe-cli deploy dashboard_seeds 1
```

## Rules for writing good graphs

1. Prefer explicit kwargs (`call("http_request", url=base)`) over positional args.
2. Build URLs with `+` concatenation, never f-strings.
3. Read config from env (`env.template`/`env.get` with `default`) — never hardcode credentials.
4. Split reusable units into subgraphs; keep a parent graph thin and sequential.
5. Name subgraphs with a domain prefix (`seed_`, `process_`, `report_`).
6. Use `META(...)` for title/SLA/tags; use `GROUP("...")` to structure readable plan dumps.
7. Keep loop bodies minimal — every iteration re-executes the body nodes.
8. Validate with `check` before `create`; expect failures at runtime to be visible in
   `executions list/show` with per-node steps.

### Kuruş-int rule (money is integer kuruş)

The type system is `int`/`float` only — there is no Decimal/money type. Money amounts are
always integer **kuruş** (100 kuruş = 1 TL): store, compute and return amounts as `int`
(e.g. `price = 2499` means 24.99 TL), never as `float`. If a computation involves division,
round back to integer kuruş at the boundary — the money value itself must never be a float.
Name money variables with a `_kurus` (or `_cents`) suffix so the unit is explicit:
`vat_kurus`, `total_cents`.
